title: Streaming-weighted input/output pricing trial + enterprise security QA checklist
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Background: Customers have divergent cost sensitivities for input (prompt) tokens vs output (generation) tokens, and streaming sessions can produce irregular per-request billing spikes. Objective: Run a 4-week controlled trial of a streaming-weighted per-token pricing model that assigns configurable weight factors to ingress and egress tokens, plus a per-session streaming graceband that smooths low-volume burst charges. The experiment couples pricing logic with an enterprise security contract addendum and a short security questionnaire to ensure visibility on billing behavior for high-SLA customers. Hypothesis: Introducing a modest input:output weight (e.g., 0.6 ingress / 1.0 egress) with a small per-session graceband (first 30 output tokens free of egress weight) will lead to lower churn for prompt-heavy workloads without materially reducing net hosted revenue (> -5% revenue delta). Success metrics: 1) Churn lift on trial cohorts (delta > +3% retention over 30d), 2) Revenue delta vs control within +-5%, 3) Median tail latency change < +5ms, 4) No increase in fraud/abuse signals above baseline. Experiment groups: - Control: current symmetric per-token pricing - Variant A: weighted IO (0.6 ingress / 1.0 egress) - Variant B: weighted IO + 30-token streaming graceband - Variant C: weighted IO + per-session minimum credit smoothing (time-windowed) Implementation checklist: - Billing: add runtime flag to apply per-request weight factors and session graceband logic (ENG-ops ticket required). - SDK: document new pricing flags and expose reported effective_token_units in response metadata. - Console: add experiment toggle on project billing page and delta preview for sample request traces. - Telemetry: emit per-request effective_units, raw_ingress_tokens, raw_egress_tokens, session_id, and billing_bucket. - Reporting: nightly cohort reports for revenue/retention by cohort. - Legal/Sales: draft enterprise contract addendum language describing graceband and how minimums are applied; prepare FAQ for sales. - Security/Compliance: complete short enterprise security questionnaire entry on billing determinism and audit logs (see Security tasks below). Rollout plan: 1) Internal alpha (Redwood internal projects only, 2 weeks) 2) Small external pilot (10 customers across prompt-heavy, balanced, and gen-heavy profiles, 4 weeks) 3) Monitor metrics and iterate, then either scale to opt-in flag or revert. Risks and mitigations: - Revenue downside: apply gradual exposure caps and reserve a rollback plan. - Customer confusion: provide clear per-request examples and estimated invoice preview in Console. - Fraud/abuse: rate-limit new per-session smoothers and add anomaly detection. - Accounting reconciliation: run parallel metering pipeline to ensure billing parity. Links: design notes (drive://rwd/design/pricing-graceband-v1), PRD (confluence://rdw/Hosted-Pricing-IO-Graceband), telemetry dashboards (grafana://rwd/hosted/pricing-experiments), draft addendum (drive://rwd/legal/enterprise-pricing-addendum-draft).
